review_notes:
I read the whole file. I also grepped the other consumers of `taylorCoeffAt`: LaurentCoeff, Residue, PrincipalPart and PlanarTrace.

The only candidate for bundling is the ℂ-linearity group: `taylorCoeffAt_add`, `_const_mul`, `_neg`, `_sub`, `_fun_sum`. These lemmas hold only on analytic germs, so a bundle would need a domain such as a submodule or subalgebra of germs. Mathlib has no such object for this `ℂ → ℂ` setting, so the bundle would be new infrastructure.

Existing consumers use the unbundled lemmas directly. Examples are `taylorCoeffAt_fun_add` and `taylorCoeffAt_const_mul` in LaurentCoeff, and `taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul` in LaurentCoeff and PrincipalPart. A bundled `LinearMap` would add coercions and membership proofs and would not clearly simplify any of them.

`taylorCoeffAt` itself is already a plain iterate of a named operator, with a bridge to `p.coeff`. I found no clear bundling improvement that would materially simplify an existing consumer.
